questions.question: What was the day of the week on 18 March 2020?
questions.solution:
We need to find the day for **18 March 2020**.

Completed years (2000 years + 19 years) + period from **1 January 2020 to 18 March 2020**.

**1. Odd days in 2000 years:**

As 2000 is a multiple of 400 ⇒ **0 odd days**.

**2. Odd days in the remaining 19 years (2001 to 2019):**

In 19 years, number of **leap years** = 19/4 = **4** (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016).

Number of **ordinary years** = 19 − 4 = 15.

Odd days = (4 × 2) + (15 × 1) = 8 + 15 = 23 days.

23 days = (23 ÷ 7) ⇒ 3 weeks + **2 odd days**.

**3. Odd days in 2020 (up to 18 March):**

2020 is a **leap year** (divisible by 4).

January = 31 days

February = 29 days

March = 18 days

Total days = 31 + 29 + 18 = 78 days.

78 days = (78 ÷ 7) ⇒ 11 weeks + **1 odd day**.

**4. Total odd days:**

Total odd days = 0 (from 2000 years) + 2 (from 19 years) + 1 (from 2020) = **3 odd days**.

**5. Mapping of the day:**

According to the **odd days** count: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday, 3 = **Wednesday**, 4 = Thursday, 5 = Friday, 6 = Saturday.

Since the total number of odd days is 3, the day was **Wednesday**.

The day on 18 March 2020 is Wednesday.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__

Using the formula: Day = (Date + Month Code + Century Code + Year + Year/4) ÷ 7

For **18 March 2020**:

Date = 18

Month Code (March) = 4

Century Code (2000) = 6

Year = 20

Leap Year (20 ÷ 4) = 5

Total = 18 + 4 + 6 + 20 + 5 = 53

53 ÷ 7 ⇒ Remainder = **4**

In this system (where 1 = Sunday, 2 = Monday, 3 = Tuesday, 4 = Wednesday), the code 4 corresponds to **Wednesday**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Wednesday**.

questions.question: What will be the sum of number of days in the month of June, February, July and August in the year 2300?
questions.solution:
Checking the **year 2300**:

2300 ÷ 100 = 23 (It is a **century year**)

2300 ÷ 400 = 5.75

Since 2300 is a century year but is not divisible by 400, it is a **common year**.

Now, we list the number of days for each month in 2300:

Days in **June** = 30

Days in **February** (common year) = 28

Days in **July** = 31

Days in **August** = 31

Sum of the number of days = 30 + 28 + 31 + 31

Sum = 58 + 62

Sum = **120**

Hence, the sum of the number of days in the month of **June**, **February**, **July**, and **August** in the **year 2300** is **120**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively. A third pipe can empty the tank in 9 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours.

A third pipe can empty the tank in 9 hours. 

**Formula used:**

Time = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let pipes are A, B and C.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 36 ÷ 12 = **3 units/hr**

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 36 ÷ 18 = **2 units/hr**

Efficiency of **Pipe C** = 36 ÷ 9 = **4 units/hr** (Since it empties the tank, its efficiency will be taken as negative).

Net Efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

Net Efficiency = 3 + 2 − 4 = **1 unit/hr**

Time = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

Time = 36 ÷ 1 = **36 hours**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

questions.question: The maximum number of ministers in the Union Council of Ministers is restricted to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The size of the **Union Council of Ministers** was formally limited by the **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**. Before this amendment, there was no specific numerical limit on the number of ministers, which often led to the formation of large cabinets for political convenience.
 
• According to **Article 75 (1A)** of the **Indian Constitution**, the total number of ministers, including the **Prime Minister**, in the **Union Council of Ministers** shall not exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People).
 
• This constitutional provision aims to ensure administrative efficiency, reduce the burden on the **exchequer**, and maintain the sanctity of the **cabinet system** by preventing jumbo ministries.
 
• Based on the current strength of the **Lok Sabha**, which is **543** elected members, the maximum permissible number of ministers at the central level is **81**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Provisions for State Governments:**

 
 
• Similar to the Union level, **Article 164 (1A)** restricts the size of the **Council of Ministers** in a State. The number of ministers, including the **Chief Minister**, cannot exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **Legislative Assembly** of that State.
 
• For smaller states, the law provides a minimum threshold where the number of ministers shall not be less than **12**.
 
 
 
• **Specific Exception for Delhi:**
 
 
• Under the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991**, the **National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi** follows a different rule. **Article 239AA** limits the number of ministers to **10%** of the total membership of the **Delhi Legislative Assembly**, resulting in a maximum of 7 ministers.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Ministers:**
 
 
• The **Council of Ministers** is a multi-tier body comprising **Cabinet Ministers** (who lead major ministries), **Ministers of State (Independent Charge)**, **Ministers of State**, and **Deputy Ministers**. The 15% limit applies to the sum of all these categories.

questions.question: Which musical instrument typically accompanies the Tippani dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhol and manjira (small cymbals)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tippani dance**, also known as **Matla Dance**, is a traditional folk dance from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, specifically the coastal areas of **Chorwad** and **Veraval**.
 
• It is primarily performed by the women of the **Koli** and **Bhil** communities, who historically used this rhythmic activity to reduce the monotony of **manual labor**.
 
• The **Dhol** (a double-headed drum) and **Manjira** (small hand cymbals) are the vital musical instruments that provide the necessary **rhythmic accompaniment** for the performers to maintain a steady tempo.
 
• The dance utilizes a unique prop called a **Tippani**, which is a long **wooden stick** (approximately 175 cm) with a square wooden or iron block called a **Garbo** attached at the end.
 
• Dancers strike the **Tippani** poles against the floor in synchronization with the beats of the **Dhol**, creating a powerful percussive sound that mimics the process of **leveling ground** or beating **limestone** for construction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Detailed Aspects of the Dance:**

 
 
• **Zanz:** Large metallic cymbals are often used alongside the **Manjira** to add depth to the musical arrangement during high-energy segments.
 
• **Chaniya Choli:** The performers wear vibrant, traditional Gujarati **folk costumes**, often featuring intricate **mirror work** and embroidery typical of the **Saurashtra** region.
 
• **Transition of Tempo:** The performance usually begins with a **slow beat** and gradually accelerates into a fast-paced finale, showcasing the physical stamina of the dancers.
 
 
 
• **Other Folk Dances of Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Garba:** A globally recognized dance performed in a circle around a **perforated clay lamp** (Garba Deep), predominantly during the **Navratri** festival.
 
• **Bhavai:** A traditional **folk theater** form where performers balance multiple **brass pitchers** on their heads while dancing.
 
• **Siddi Dhamal:** A rhythmic dance performed by the **Siddi** community (of African descent) featuring the **Dhamal** drum and unique vocal patterns.

questions.question: Which Veda is primarily known for its musical content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samaveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Samaveda** is the second of the four Vedas and is known as the **Veda of Melodies and Chants**, serving as the foundational text for **Indian Classical Music** and dance.
 
• It contains a total of **1,875 verses**, the majority of which are taken from the **Rigveda**, specifically from the 8th and 9th **Mandalas**, and rearranged for musical performance.
 
• The hymns of the Samaveda were traditionally chanted by the **Udgatar** priests during **Soma sacrifices** and other significant **Vedic rituals**.
 
• This Veda introduced the concept of the **seven musical notes** (Saptaswara), which are **Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni**, forming the core of the **Gandharva Veda** (the science of music).
 
• It is divided into two primary parts: the **Archika** (collection of hymns) and the **Gana** (songbooks that provide instructions on how the verses should be sung).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda**:

 
 
• It is the **oldest** of the four Vedas, consisting of **1,028 hymns** (Suktas) organized into **10 Mandalas**.
 
• It focuses on prayers to **nature deities** such as **Indra** (God of Thunder), **Agni** (God of Fire), and **Varuna** (God of Water).
 
 
 
• **Yajurveda**:
 
 
• Known as the **Veda of Rituals**, it contains prose mantras and instructions for performing **Yajnas** (sacrificial ceremonies).
 
• It is categorized into two versions: the **Shukla Yajurveda** (White/Pure) and the **Krishna Yajurveda** (Black/Dark).
 
 
 
• **Atharvaveda**:
 
 
• This Veda deals with **magical spells**, charms, and incantations meant to ward off evil and cure diseases.
 
• It is a crucial source for ancient **Indian medicine** (Ayurveda) and describes the **socio-cultural** life of the later Vedic period.

questions.question: Why does the moon exert less gravitational force than Earth?

options.text: It is farther from the Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has less mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, the force of attraction between two bodies is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The **mass** of the Moon is approximately **7.347 × 10²² kg**, which is roughly **1.2%** (or about 1/81) of **Earth's mass** (5.972 × 10²⁴ kg). Because gravity is a property of matter, the less matter (mass) an object has, the weaker its **gravitational pull**.
 
• The **surface gravity** of a celestial body is calculated using the formula g = (G times M)/(R²) . Although the Moon's **radius (R)** is smaller than Earth's, the significantly smaller **mass (M)** results in a lower value for **g**.
 
• The Moon's gravitational force is only about **1/6th** (approximately 1.62 m/s²) of the **gravitational force** found on Earth (9.8 m/s²). This means an object on the Moon weighs six times less than it does on Earth, even though its **mass remains constant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Influencing Gravity**

 
 
• **Mass**: This is the primary determinant of **gravitational strength**. Greater mass creates a deeper "well" in **spacetime**, exerting more force on surrounding objects.
 
• **Distance/Radius**: Gravity weakens as the **distance** from the center of mass increases. While the Moon is smaller in **size**, its low mass outweighs the effect of having a smaller radius.
 
• **Rotation Speed**: The **rotational velocity** of a planet or moon creates **centrifugal force**, which slightly counteracts gravity at the equator, but it does not change the actual **gravitational force** generated by mass.
 
• **Sun's Influence**: The distance from the **Sun** affects the orbital path of the Earth-Moon system but does not dictate the **local gravity** experienced on the surface of the Moon itself.

questions.question: Who is the author of The Palace of Illusions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni** is a renowned **Indian-American author**, poet, and the **Betty and Gene McDavid Professor of Creative Writing** at the **University of Houston**.
 
• **The Palace of Illusions**, published in **2008**, is her award-winning novel that provides a first-person retelling of the **Mahabharata** from the perspective of **Draupadi** (Panchaali).
 
• The novel is significant for its **feminist interpretation** of the patriarchal epic, exploring **Draupadi's** childhood, her marriage to the five **Pandavas**, her complicated relationship with **Karna**, and her spiritual bond with **Krishna**.
 
• Through this work, the author reimagines the **Kurukshetra War** and the events leading up to it, focusing on the internal emotional world and agency of the female protagonist.
 
• Apart from this book, she is well-known for **The Mistress of Spices**, **Before We Visit the Goddess**, and **The Forest of Enchantments** (a retelling of the **Ramayana** from **Sita's** perspective).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sudha Murthy**:

 
 
• An Indian educator, author, and philanthropist who serves as the chairperson of the **Infosys Foundation**.
 
• Her popular literary works include **Wise and Otherwise**, **Dollar Bahu**, and **The Serpent's Revenge**.
 
 
 
• **Devdutt Pattanaik**:
 
 
• A prominent Indian **mythologist** and illustrator known for his books on **Hindu mythology** and their application in modern management.
 
• His notable works include **Jaya: An Illustrated Retelling of the Mahabharata**, **Sita**, and **Mithya**.
 
 
 
• **Kavita Kane**:

questions.question: Earth's magnetic field protects us from charged solar particles. What happens when Earth's magnetic field weakens temporarily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased auroras and radiation risk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Magnetosphere** acts as Earths primary protective shield, generated by the **geodynamo effect** within the liquid **outer core**, which deflects the **solar wind** and **galactic cosmic radiation** away from the planet.
 
• During periods of temporary weakening, such as **geomagnetic excursions** or the early stages of a **polar reversal**, the magnetic field intensity can drop by up to **90%**, significantly reducing its shielding capacity.
 
• A weakened field allows high-energy **charged particles** from the Sun to penetrate deeper into the **ionosphere** and **thermosphere**, leading to the appearance of **auroras** (Northern and Southern Lights) at much **lower latitudes** than usual.
 
• Increased **solar particle flux** elevates the **radiation risk** for high-altitude aviation, space missions, and can induce **geomagnetic currents** that threaten **electrical power grids** and **global navigation satellite systems (GNSS)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geomagnetic Reversals**:

 
 
• These are long-term events where the **magnetic North and South poles** swap positions; the last major reversal was the **Brunhes-Matuyama reversal** roughly **780,000 years ago**.
 
• Scientific data from the **Laschamp event** (approx. 41,000 years ago) suggests that even brief weakenings can impact **ozone layer stability** due to increased nitric oxide production.
 
 
 
• **South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA)**:
 
 
• A current region where Earths magnetic field is significantly weaker than the global average, exposing **satellites** to higher levels of **ionizing radiation** and potential hardware malfunctions.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric vs. Gravitational Stability**:
 
 
• A **complete loss of atmosphere** requires sustained stripping by solar wind over millions of years (similar to **Mars**), not a temporary magnetic dip.
 
• **Gravity** is a function of Earths **mass** and **universal gravitational constant**, making it entirely independent of **electromagnetism**.

questions.question: Before 1991, which policy limited private sector participation in certain industries?

__
 
• The **Industrial Licensing Policy** was a central feature of India's economic framework established under the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**, creating a system often referred to as the **License Raj**.
 
• Under this policy, private entrepreneurs were legally required to obtain a government **license** to start a new industrial undertaking, expand existing production capacity, or diversify into new product lines.
 
• The primary objective of this restrictive policy was to ensure that **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** dominated the **commanding heights of the economy**, effectively barring or limiting private participation in strategic sectors like heavy machinery and telecommunications.
 
• It served as a tool for the state to manage **scarce resources**, prevent the concentration of economic wealth, and promote **regional development** by incentivizing industries in backward areas.
 
• The **New Economic Policy of 1991** dismantled this regime by abolishing licensing for the majority of industries, marking a shift toward **Liberalization** and increased private sector involvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Trade Policy**:

 
 
• Before 1991, India followed an **Inward-Oriented** strategy characterized by **Import Substitution** and high **import tariffs**.
 
• It aimed to protect domestic **Infant Industries** from international competition through strict **quantitative restrictions** and quotas.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Subsidy Policy**:
 
 
• This involves government financial aid provided to farmers for inputs such as **fertilizers**, **electricity**, and irrigation to ensure **food security**.
 
• It focuses on maintaining the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** rather than regulating industrial entry.
 
 
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS)**:
 
 
• A food security system established by the **Government of India** to distribute essential commodities like wheat, rice, and kerosene to the poor at **subsidized rates**.

questions.question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for changes in males during puberty?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Testosterone** is the primary **androgen** (male sex hormone) secreted by the **Leydig cells** located in the **interstitial spaces** of the **testes**.
 
• During **puberty**, the **hypothalamus** releases **Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)**, which stimulates the **anterior pituitary gland** to secrete **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** and **Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)**.
 
• **LH** specifically triggers the production of **testosterone**, which is responsible for the development of **secondary sexual characteristics** in males.
 
• Key physical changes include the growth of **facial, axillary, and pubic hair**, as well as the **broadening of shoulders** and increased **muscle mass**.
 
• It promotes the enlargement of the **larynx** (voice box), resulting in a significantly **deeper voice**.
 
• **Testosterone** is vital for the maturation of **male reproductive organs**, including the **scrotum**, **testes**, and **penis**, and is essential for **spermatogenesis** (sperm production).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oestrogen**:

 
 
• Produced primarily by the **ovaries** in females.
 
• Responsible for female **secondary sexual characteristics** like **breast development** and **hip widening**.
 
• Plays a critical role in regulating the **menstrual cycle** and maintaining the **uterine lining**.
 
 
 
• **Thyroxin**:
 
 
• Secreted by the **thyroid gland** located in the neck region.
 
• Contains **iodine** and is responsible for regulating the **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)** and the metabolism of **carbohydrates, proteins, and fats**.
 
 
 
• **Adrenaline**:
 
 
• Secreted by the **adrenal medulla** of the **adrenal glands**.
 
• Known as the **emergency hormone** or **fight-or-flight** hormone, it increases **heart rate**, **blood pressure**, and **blood glucose levels** during stress.

__
 
• The international border between **India** and **Bangladesh** is approximately **4,096.7 km** long, making it the longest land boundary India shares with any of its neighbors.
 
• The Indian states that share a land border with Bangladesh include **West Bengal**, **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.

• **West Bengal** shares the most extensive boundary with Bangladesh, measuring roughly **2,217 km**, which accounts for more than half of the total border length. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge of Indian agriculture today?

options.text: Sparse rural population density limiting farm labor
Progressive fragmentation and declining size of operational holdings
Shrinking domestic demand for staple food grains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Progressive fragmentation and declining size of operational holdings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A major structural challenge in Indian agriculture is the **progressive fragmentation** of land, which is primarily caused by the **laws of inheritance** and the sub-division of ancestral property among multiple heirs over generations.
 
• According to the **10th Agriculture Census (2015-16)**, **small and marginal holdings** (less than 2 hectares) account for approximately **86.21%** of the total number of operational holdings in India.
 
• The **average size of operational holdings** has seen a steady decline from **2.28 hectares** in 1970-71 to just **1.08 hectares** in 2015-16, making farming economically unviable for many households.
 
• Fragmentation hinders the adoption of **modern agricultural technology** and **mechanization**, as using heavy machinery like tractors or harvesters is not cost-effective on tiny, scattered plots.
 
• Small farm sizes restrict the farmer's ability to create **efficient irrigation systems**, achieve **economies of scale**, and access **formal institutional credit**, as small land parcels are often not viewed as sufficient collateral by banks.
 
• This phenomenon leads to **low agricultural productivity**, higher **input costs**, and a lack of **market surplus**, keeping a large section of the farming community in a cycle of debt and poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Analysis of incorrect options and related concepts:
 
 
• **Rural Population Density**: India does not face a sparse rural population; rather, it deals with **excessive population pressure** on land, resulting in **disguised unemployment** where more labor is engaged than necessary.
 
• **Agricultural Mechanization**: While mechanization is increasing, it is considered a **developmental objective** to improve efficiency; the challenge lies in its **uneven adoption** across small landholdings.
 
• **Domestic Demand**: With a population of over **1.4 billion**, the domestic demand for **staple food grains** like rice and wheat is growing, supported by schemes like the **National Food Security Act (NFSA)**.
 
 
 
• To counter land fragmentation, the government promotes **Land Consolidation (Chakbandi)** and the formation of **Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)** to help small farmers aggregate their resources and improve their **bargaining power** in the market.

• Living around the **1st Century AD**, he was a physician in the court of the **Kushana King Kanishka**.
 
• His work heavily emphasizes the **Tridosha theory**, which balances three bodily humors: **Vata** (wind), **Pitta** (bile), and **Kapha** (phlegm), to maintain optimal health.

questions.question: In which of the following years Aurangzeb died?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Aurangzeb**, the sixth **Mughal Emperor**, died on **3 March 1707** at the age of 88.
 
• He passed away in **Ahmednagar**, Maharashtra, during a long military campaign in the **Deccan** region.
 
• His reign lasted for nearly **49 years**, beginning in **1658** after he emerged victorious in the war of succession against his brothers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regnal Titles and Persona**:

 
 
• Aurangzeb adopted the title **Alamgir**, which translates to **Conqueror of the World**.
 
• He was often called **Zinda Pir** (the Living Saint) because of his austere lifestyle and strict adherence to **Islamic law**.
 
 
 
• **Territorial Expansion**:
 
 
• Under his rule, the **Mughal Empire** reached its maximum geographical extent, stretching across almost the entire **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• He successfully annexed the **Deccan Sultanates** of **Bijapur** (1686) and **Golconda** (1687).
 
 
 
• **Policies and Succession**:

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 68 cm. One of the diagonal is 16 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of both the diagonals of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side (a)** of rhombus = **Perimeter** ÷ 4 = 68 ÷ 4 = 17 cm.

One half-diagonal (d₁/2) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplet** (8, 15, 17): the other half-diagonal (d₂/2) = 15 cm.

Second diagonal (d₂) = 15 × 2 = 30 cm.

Sum of diagonals = 16 + 30 = 46 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** = 68 cm, **Diagonal** d₁ = 16 cm.

**Formula Used:** Side of rhombus a = Perimeter/4; Relationship: a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68d83f09b60bca8192ecb29c2e9e8b4e77a09a96178d92c582b6e75c071c6eb7.png] 

⇒ Side a = 68 ÷ 4 = 17 cm

⇒ Let half of the diagonals be h₁ and h₂.

⇒ h₁ = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

⇒ a² = h₁² + h₂²

⇒ 17² = 8² + h₂²

⇒ 289 = 64 + h₂²

⇒ h₂² = 289 − 64 = 225

⇒ h₂ = √225 = 15 cm

⇒ Second diagonal d₂ = 2 × h₂ = 2 × 15 = 30 cm

⇒ **Sum of both the diagonals** = d₁ + d₂ = 16 + 30 = 46 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All sides are equal, and diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Area of a Rhombus

Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the diagonals.

Side-Diagonal Relationship

4a² = d₁² + d₂², which is derived from the Pythagorean theorem applied to the four internal right-angled triangles.

Side of **Rhombus** (s) = **Perimeter** ÷ 4 = 68 ÷ 4 = 17 cm.

Half of the given **diagonal** (d₁/2) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

Using **Pythagoras triplet** (8, 15, 17), the half of other diagonal (d₂/2) = 8 cm.

Ratio of **diagonals** is the same as the ratio of their halves.

Required Ratio = 15 : 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** = 68 cm, **Diagonal 1** (d₁) = 30 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3e18457efcdf7bd65e518ad36bbba8a43231bc998ca427e0543483b2606fb4d.png] 

⇒ Side of **Rhombus** = 68 ÷ 4 = 17 cm

⇒ x² = 289 − 225 = 64

⇒ x = √64 = 8 cm

⇒ Second **diagonal** (d₂) = 2 × 8 = 16 cm

⇒ Ratio of **diagonals** = d₁ : d₂ = 30 : 16

⇒ Ratio = 15 : 8

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

The **diagonals** of a **rhombus** bisect each other at **right angles** (90°).

Relation between Side and Diagonals

For a **rhombus** with side 's', the relation is 4s² = d₁² + d₂².

questions.question: A man travelled for first 6 hours at the speed of 40 km/hr. He travelled for next 4 hours at the speed of 15 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = (s₁t₁ + s₂t₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂)

Average Speed = (40 × 6 + 15 × 4) ÷ (6 + 4)

Average Speed = (240 + 60) ÷ 10 = 300 ÷ 10

Average Speed = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ = 40 km/hr, Time₁ = 6 hr

Speed₂ = 15 km/hr, Time₂ = 4 hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = **Speed × Time**

Average Speed = **Total Distance ÷ Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a44145a3b52a42e5d7e976615d02dfd484072bd5a4ec9cc82dc70bc57c41807c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in first 6 hr = 40 × 6 = 240 km

⇒ Distance covered in next 4 hr = 15 × 4 = 60 km

⇒ Total distance = 240 + 60 = 300 km

⇒ Total time taken = 6 + 4 = 10 hr

⇒ Average speed = 300 ÷ 10 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time)

When a person travels for two equal time intervals at speeds x and y, the average speed is (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.question: A train crosses a standing pole in 20 seconds and a platform of length 400 metre in 40 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The extra distance covered is the **length of the platform**.

Extra time taken = 40 sec − 20 sec = 20 sec

**Speed** = (Length of platform) ÷ (Extra time taken)

Speed = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to cross **pole** (t₁) = 20 sec

Time to cross **platform** (t₂) = 40 sec

Length of **platform** (Lₚ) = 400 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e75a8f58c324b3f4cae05ef075eb9fd6a6d9de15bf48ee897e0d1e8ef83d0992.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **length of the train** be L.

⇒ Speed (v) when crossing a pole = L ÷ 20

⇒ Speed (v) when crossing a platform = (L + 400) ÷ 40

⇒ Since speed is constant: L ÷ 20 = (L + 400) ÷ 40

⇒ 40L = 20(L + 400)

⇒ 2L = L + 400

⇒ L = 400 m

⇒ Speed (v) = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing Different Objects

When a train crosses a **stationary point object** (pole, man, tree), distance = length of train. When it crosses an **object with length** (platform, bridge, another train), distance = length of train + length of object.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. If they move in the **same direction**, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

questions.question: If (4x + 3y) : (4x - 3y) = 5 : 2, then what is the value of x : y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Componendo and Dividendo** rule: If (a + b) / (a − b) = c / d, then a / b = (c + d) / (c − d).

Here, a = 4x, b = 3y, c = 5, and d = 2.

4x / 3y = (5 + 2) / (5 − 2) = 7 / 3

x / y = (7 / 3) × (3 / 4) = 7 / 4

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The ratio of **linear combinations** (4x + 3y) : (4x − 3y) = 5 : 2.

**Formula Used:** Cross-multiplication method for **proportions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a6c78a78ea9d001be3b991cf31c0f19cf190088d908555eddc83deb9483d495.png] 

⇒ (4x + 3y) / (4x − 3y) = 5 / 2

⇒ 2 × (4x + 3y) = 5 × (4x − 3y)

⇒ 8x + 6y = 20x − 15y

⇒ 6y + 15y = 20x − 8x

⇒ 21y = 12x

⇒ x / y = 21 / 12

⇒ x / y = 7 / 4

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 4.**

questions.question: Four numbers are in the ratio of 1 : 3 : 5 : 4. Sum of these numbers is 52. What is the difference between the largest and smallest number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts = 1 + 3 + 5 + 4 = 13 units.

Given 13 units = 52 ⇒ 1 unit = 52 ÷ 13 = 4.

Difference between **largest** (5) and **smallest** (1) parts = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Required difference = 4 units × 4 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = 1 : 3 : 5 : 4 and **Sum** = 52.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a5ab56cf35b36a476d56d85e56baebc23589bb019b7b1ada4151c03a0be874b.png] 

**Formula Used:** Sum of terms = Total value

⇒ Let the four numbers be 1x, 3x, 5x, and 4x.

⇒ 1x + 3x + 5x + 4x = 52

⇒ 13x = 52

⇒ x = 52 ÷ 13 = 4

⇒ **Smallest number** (1x) = 1 × 4 = 4

⇒ **Largest number** (5x) = 5 × 4 = 20

⇒ **Difference** = 20 − 4 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

Ratio Distribution Rule

To find the value of any part, multiply the **Total Value** by (Part Ratio ÷ Sum of all Ratio Parts).

Proportionality Constant

The variable x represents the **Common Multiplier** that scales the ratio parts to their actual values.

Difference between Parts

The difference between any two numbers in a ratio can be calculated directly by finding the difference in their **ratio units** first.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 120 percent of its cost price. Its selling price is 90 percent of the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Markup percentage** = +20% and **Discount percentage** = −10% (since SP is 90% of MP).

Net change formula: a + b + (ab/100)

Net Profit % = 20 − 10 − (20 × 10)/100

Net Profit % = 10 − 2 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price** (MP) = 120% of **Cost Price** (CP)

**Selling Price** (SP) = 90% of **Marked Price** (MP)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1bdd83a30030009495e5b2c5a3f9c63f74e5ffbf5403d919e7af2780ddf1c91.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Cost Price** (CP) = 100

⇒ **Marked Price** (MP) = 120% of 100 = 120

⇒ **Selling Price** (SP) = 90% of MP

⇒ SP = (90/100) × 120 = 108

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 108 − 100 = 8

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit/CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (8/100) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price. Markup % = (MP − CP)/CP × 100.

Discount Percentage

It is the reduction offered on the marked price. Discount % = (MP − SP)/MP × 100.

Relationship between CP and MP

CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%). This direct ratio is useful for finding any one unknown variable.

questions.question: If (x + 3) : 40 :: 12 : 20, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Observe the relationship between the **second** and **fourth** terms in the **proportion**.

The fourth term (20) × 2 = The second term (40).

Applying the same **factor** to the third term: 12 × 2 = 24.

Thus, x + 3 = 24

x = 24 − 3 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (x + 3) : 40 :: 12 : 20

**Formula Used:** In a **proportion** a : b :: c : d, the product of **extremes** equals the product of **means** (a × d = b × c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e40297bb5bf3995bd785111d9e5d635905dfa966112b7fe1a705125797d5f683.png] 

⇒ (x + 3) × 20 = 40 × 12

⇒ 20x + 60 = 480

⇒ 20x = 480 − 60

⇒ 20x = 420

⇒ x = 420 ÷ 20

⇒ x = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Extremes and Means

In a proportion a : b = c : d, the terms 'a' and 'd' are called **extremes**, while 'b' and 'c' are called **means**. The fundamental property is a × d = b × c.

Mean Proportional

If a, b, c are in **continued proportion**, then a : b :: b : c, which implies b² = a × c. Here, 'b' is the **mean proportional**.

Fourth Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are given, the **fourth proportional** 'd' is calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.
